claims.text: The WTaTiVZr alloy is equimolar, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% each of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr.
The processed WTaTiVZr alloy has a nanocrystalline BCC or similar solid-solution microstructure.
The nanocrystalline WTaTiVZr microstructure contains a high density of grain boundaries.
Severe lattice distortion from the multi-principal-element composition stabilizes the nanocrystalline grain boundaries.
Severe lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr produces an ultrafine-grained microstructure.
At elevated temperature, the grain boundaries in WTaTiVZr become active deformation sites that enable substantial grain-boundary sliding and related boundary-mediated plasticity.
Boundary-mediated deformation reduces dislocation pile-up in WTaTiVZr.
Reducing dislocation pile-up delays crack nucleation and propagation in WTaTiVZr.
The proposed grain-boundary mechanism gives WTaTiVZr greater plastic strain capacity than pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
The proposed grain-boundary mechanism gives WTaTiVZr greater toughness or work of fracture than pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
Pure tungsten under the proposed conditions remains dislocation-dominated and susceptible to dislocation pile-up.
Commercial pure tungsten is expected to show limited plasticity and toughness with brittle cleavage-type fracture under the proposed high-temperature conditions.
Temperatures around 1000 °C or higher are above tungsten's typical ductile-to-brittle transition.
Pure tungsten normally exhibits brittle behavior in the stated temperature regime above its ductile-to-brittle transition.
WTaTiVZr should exhibit a statistically significant increase in plastic strain to failure relative to pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr should exhibit statistically higher toughness or work of fracture than pure tungsten.
Deformed WTaTiVZr should show predominant grain-boundary sliding and reduced dislocation activity relative to pure tungsten.
Prolonged high-temperature exposure may evolve the WTaTiVZr microstructure and alter the proposed effect.
Both materials will be tested under nominally identical high-temperature loading conditions, with pure tungsten serving as the control.
Failure to observe both improved mechanical outcomes and a shift toward grain-boundary-mediated plasticity is designated as a falsifying result.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis places testing above tungsten's ductile-to-brittle transition while simultaneously defining that regime as one in which tungsten normally remains brittle and cleavage-prone. Above the transition would ordinarily denote the more ductile side of the transition, so the stated boundary and baseline are internally inconsistent.
